assessments.scope: Oversight of a more capable system by a non-expert human or a weaker model on tasks outside the Khan et al. 2024 setting and outside the Lean theorem's abstract oracle protocol

nodes.text: Broad reading of the debate literature: debate lets non-expert humans and weaker models oversee more capable systems. Source anchors are the Khan et al. abstract sentence on the viability of aligning models with debate in the absence of ground truth and Theorem 6.2 of arXiv:2311.14125v1. The claim is OPEN because it rests on three assumptions recorded as separate nodes: that agents can play the assumed strategies, that the judge verifies what the results assume, and that the results transfer to the target tasks. Nothing in this pack establishes it.
nodes.title: Application claim: debate lets non-experts and weaker models oversee more capable systems

nodes.text: The formal results prescribe strategies: Theorem 6.2 of arXiv:2311.14125v1 and the pinned Lean correctness theorem fix honest Alice, Bob and Vera strategies (Params.defaults) and quantify over dishonest opponents within fixed types. The experiment reports that LLM debaters, often through poor quote selection, are the bottleneck (Insight 9, App. B.1) and used best-of-N, critique-and-refinement and Elo selection to approach stronger play. Whether agents in a target deployment can play the assumed strategies is unestablished.
nodes.title: Assumption: agents can play the strategies the results assume

source_refs.locator: lines 28-34 (vera p.c p.s p.v argument of Correct)

nodes.text: In the Lean formalization the verifier Vera checks Alice's claimed probability by sampling the oracle with prescribed parameters, and Theorem 6.2's verifier is described in the paper as querying the stochastic oracle; whether that access corresponds to Lean's Vera sampling is open (obligation D03), and both sides assume exact verification of the queried quantity. Khan et al.'s judges instead rely on a quote tool that marks verified and unverified quotes, and the paper reports verbosity bias, positional bias, overconfidence of LLM judges and underconfidence of human judges (Sec. 4, App. A.7). Whether a target judge verifies what either result assumes is unestablished.
nodes.title: Assumption: the judge verifies what the results assume

nodes.text: Khan et al. limit their results to setups where the debaters can provide verified evidence to the judge, note that the models were RLHF-tuned and honest-leaning so that suitability for deceptive models is unclear, and leave generalisation to domains needing larger evidence sets or parametric knowledge open (Sec. 6). The Lean theorem is correctness-only for an abstract finite oracle protocol and carries no language, machine or resource content. Transfer to a target task is unestablished.
nodes.title: Assumption: the results transfer to the target tasks
